# Projects and public work — background

Not book content. Background so chapters can refer to real work accurately.
**The book is not for a technical audience and should stay non-technical**
(author's instruction). Use this for grounding, not for detail.

## Rounds — the one that matters to the argument

Medical education platform. Began as gamified board preparation (Step 1),
expanding toward helping students perform confidently on rounds and as
clinicians.

**The gap the author identified, in his words:** medical education tooling
was designed for a past era of textbooks and videos. Modern practice is rapid
flashcards plus very high-volume practice questions. The result is students
regurgitating memorized sentence fragments without intuitive understanding of
what connects the fragments. The missing layer is that connective
understanding. Methodology is Duolingo-inspired.

**Why this is structurally important to the book:** this is Chapter Nine's
argument, one stage earlier in the pipeline. Ch9 says decomposing a patient
into a problem list can lose the person because meaning lives in the
relationships between findings. Rounds identifies the identical failure in
how the knowledge itself is taught — decomposed, drilled, never reassembled.
The author built the fix for the education version before articulating the
clinical version in this book. That connection is now made explicit in Ch17,
with a forward pointer at the end of Ch9.

Related repos: `roundsapp-landing`, `RoundsWebTools`, `rounds-its`,
`rounds-voice`.

## Scale

Roughly 79 repositories on the account. That volume is itself evidence for
the Ch3 and Ch17 argument about not waiting for permission — considerably
better evidence than any assertion, and available without a single technical
detail. Worth one sentence somewhere; not worth a list.
